answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by granting influence only through a verifiable work-history ledger: a new identity starts at zero weight and must complete a sequence of time-locked, independently checkable tasks — for example auditing a lagoon sensor dataset, routing a river logistics plan, and verifying a tundra supply manifest — each stamped by unrelated peers. Creating thousands of fakes then costs thousands of sequential work-hours, not just key generation, while one honest agent earns weight once and keeps it by behaving well.
